title: Tolkien Studies, Philology, and Original Mythopoeia
purpose: Teach literary analysis, historical philology, comparative mythology, language construction, worldbuilding systems, and original creative design using rights-cleared materials without ingesting copyrighted Tolkien text.

source_families.scope: Public-domain Old English primary texts and editions; verify edition and translation rights individually
Public-domain Old Norse primary texts; verify modern editions and translations individually
Public-domain folklore and Kalevala source materials; verify translation rights individually
Bibliographic metadata and authorized scholarly summaries; full articles require license review
Official bibliographic and contextual reference pages; no full-text ingestion
Only specific materials with explicit permission and documented scope

lessons: Old English and Old Norse morphology
curriculum.practice: Analyze short rights-cleared public-domain passages and explain linguistic evidence
Compare public-domain myth motifs without copying protected expression
Create an original language with a documented grammar and lexicon
Build an original world bible with internally consistent maps, timelines, and cultures

lessons: point of view and narrative distance
curriculum.practice: Outline an original multi-perspective narrative and test continuity
Write a sourced critical analysis using rights-cleared scholarship

lessons: sound and music as narrative systems
curriculum.practice: Compare high-level adaptation choices without reproducing scripts or protected dialogue
Create a wholly original myth cycle, avoiding Tolkien characters, names, maps, languages, and distinctive plot expression

assessment.holdout_policy: Keep benchmark texts separate from study materials and do not train on holdouts
assessment.mastery_claims: No mastery claim until independent scored evidence and rights review exist

safeguards: Do not ingest Tolkien novels, appendices, letters, or copyrighted translations without a specific license.
Do not reproduce distinctive characters, names, maps, languages, or protected passages.
Keep public-domain status at the edition/translation level, not merely the ancient-work level.
Use original examples and independent benchmarks.
